# Monkey Rally corresponding source

Fixed original: https://github.com/antila/ludum-dare-28/tree/79abaad33db0e0b5bddf4500800de881e2bc738c

The `upstream/` directory contains only the approved publication package. All first-party game modules, maps, CSS and original artwork are unchanged. The first-party LICENSE is CC-BY-4.0. Anders Antila wrote the code; Erik Nahkala and Laura Kantti created the art and graphics. Raxl Snaxel's music credit remains in the original credits illustration, but no soundtrack is distributed or loaded.

`publication-manifest.json` records exact byte sizes, SHA-256 and Git-blob SHA-1 for every approved input. The readable Phaser 1.1.3 / Pixi bundle has six bounded utility replacements described and hashed in `clean-engine-manifest.json`. Its output SHA-256 is `2659d5886eff76a5802376f478701234b6200ab207a57cb6aa2d5ef89e4330b6`; the approved bundle is copied verbatim into the runtime. It retains 1,151,718 original bytes (99.58%). Phaser rendering, sprites, tilemaps, input, scenes and tween machinery are retained.

The original engine's provenance is the Monkey Rally commit and Git blob `b7fa9843ee2f4e8afb56f252dd39361b8c9f8318`, rather than an assertion that it exactly equals a separately published Phaser tag. `supplement-manifest.json` records license-source identities. Full terms for Phaser, Pixi, PolyK, QuadTree, JS Signals, Tween.js/Penner, EventTarget, jQuery-derived utilities, Nonsense inspiration and Alea/Mash are under `upstream/licenses/`. The original excluded utility bodies and music/font data are not included anywhere in this package.

Preferred editable forms are the readable original JS, Tiled JSON maps, the original supplied PNG/JPEG art, readable cleaned engine, `public/monkey-rally/adapter.js`, CSS/HTML, `src/games/MonkeyRallyOriginal.tsx`, and the Python source/packaging scripts. No layered art source was supplied upstream. Generated copies are reproduced by `python3 scripts/monkey-rally/adapt.py`; this static script only copies bytes and replaces the documented source seams. There is no install or upstream build step.

## Changes, 2026-10-10

- The new GPL-3.0-only iframe adapter owns a 1280×720 original Phaser canvas, responsive outside-canvas touch controls, keyboard focus, localized captions and host selection/completion messages. React only mounts and disposes that frame.
- Host listener setup and iframe load both request an idempotent ready handshake, covering cached documents. Disposal is deferred by one microtask and guarded by the host effect epoch, so React StrictMode's synchronous effect replay cannot destroy a still-owned frame; an actual unmount still disposes its exact old window.
- Original command construction, deletion, queue sprites, entity parsing, reset-door and global reversible toggle functions are retained. The execution seam uses the same four directions, 150ms Phaser slide tween, original stop/hole/wall/goal IDs and authored maps. Blocked commands advance once per engine frame, avoiding recursive stack growth. Sequence exhaustion is visible.
- Stop and reset mark active and pending tweens for cancellation and invalidate callback generations. Stop retains the queue, resets every color and restores the start. Reset additionally clears it. Winning waits for a guarded 550ms celebration callback; navigation/disposal invalidates it.
- Pausing uses Phaser's paused flag with independent host/manual/visibility/focus reasons. Pending tween additions receive the same clock compensation as active tweens. Resume continues the exact interrupted movement. Canvas input is disabled while paused so Phaser's historical click-to-resume shortcut cannot override host pause.
- Map data is cloned before use because the old Phaser cache shares mutable layers. Original tile layers remain Phaser TilemapLayers. Additional GIDs and Tiled objects use the retained Phaser sprite renderer, their actual firstgid and authored 64/128/640px sheet sizes. No custom renderer or replacement engine was introduced.
- Leaving the visible 16×9 authored laboratory area becomes a visible failed attempt. No wall or map data is inserted. All nonzero authored gameplay entities in this eight-map campaign are inside those bounds.
- A single validated, try/catch-protected progress key stores earned level numbers. Original unscoped localStorage reads/writes and clear-save bug are removed. All stages are selectable; choosing one is never completion. The host owns each selected level before it starts.
- Original title/menu, all ten illustrated narrative panels, original credits and actual level-eight ending remain. Full credits are also readable text. Music/font loads and audio decode gates are removed; a self-only content policy blocks external assets and connections.

## Campaign count and verification

There are exactly eight genuinely authored playable puzzle maps, not fifteen unused button images or eleven narrative images counted as levels. The first, middle and final browser routes were manually derived from the maps: level 1 `UR`; level 5 `LURDLDRULD`; level 8 `LLURDRRULDRULDLU`. No solver, game state writer or injected win is used by the single targeted E2E.

The E2E covers physical keyboard and touch button input, ten story panels, queue editing, blocked directions, a mid-slide pause/resume, continuous movement, stop/reset, level-two fall, reversible red toggles, all three final-stage colors, the stop pad, actual ending, host selection alignment, interrupted callbacks, persisted completion/reentry, unrelated storage, external requests and screenshots. Static source/hash/JS syntax checks were run during preparation. Browser execution and screenshot review are explicitly pending the integrating owner's independently reviewed CI run; no pass is claimed here.

The checked release configuration uses `npm run dev -- --port 4173` as the Playwright web server and wraps App in React StrictMode. The targeted journey therefore exercises development effect replay through normal mounting, and additionally covers three rapid physical catalog exit/reentry cycles, a late ready-handshake observer, and rejection of status-only messages with the exact old frame/session. No completion message is injected. These are authored checks pending CI, not claimed execution evidence. If the integrating owner changes the server to production preview, StrictMode replay must no longer be claimed as exercised.
